meta.released.label: Released
meta.released.definition: Date the weights (or, if earlier, the technical report) were first made public, YYYY-MM-DD, as dated by the publisher. A Hugging Face repository creation date is used only when no dated publisher page exists, with a note.

meta.license.label: License
meta.license.definition: License of the released weights as declared by the publisher (model card metadata or license file), e.g. apache-2.0, mit, or the name of a custom license.

meta.modality.label: Input modalities
meta.modality.definition: Input modalities of the released checkpoint as the publisher states them, from: text, image, video, audio, joined with ' + ' in that order ("text", "text + image + video").

params.total.label: Total params
params.total.definition: Total parameter count as reported by the publisher. See params.note for whether embeddings, MTP heads or vision towers are included.

params.active.label: Active params
params.active.definition: Parameters used per token in the forward pass, as reported by the publisher.

params.active_prefill.label: Active params (prefill)
params.active_prefill.definition: Parameters used per prompt token during prefill when the publisher states it differs from decode (e.g. YOCO-style designs that skip the upper half of the stack).

params.active_non_embedding.label: Active non-embedding (stated)
params.active_non_embedding.definition: Active parameters excluding the input embedding and the output head (unembedding). Stated by the publisher, or computed from params.active by subtracting vocab × d_model for each of the embedding and output head that params.active is stated to include (basis inferred, note with the arithmetic). Not disclosed when the scope of params.active is not stated.

params.counted_total.label: Counted total params
params.counted_total.definition: Parameters of the text backbone counted from the released checkpoint's safetensors headers (embedding, output head, all experts and other weights; excluding MTP modules, vision/audio towers and n-gram lookup tables). Shown only when the counts reproduce the publisher's stated total and active parameters within 5% under some scope.

params.counted_embedding.label: Counted embedding + head
params.counted_embedding.definition: Input embedding plus output head (once if tied), counted from the checkpoint.

params.counted_lookup.label: Counted lookup tables
params.counted_lookup.definition: Parameters in n-gram / Engram / per-layer embedding tables counted from the checkpoint. Like the token embedding, they are lookups and are excluded from params.counted_total and params.counted_active_non_embedding.

params.counted_non_embedding.label: Non-emb. params (counted)
params.counted_non_embedding.definition: Language backbone weights excluding input embeddings, output head, lookup/Engram tables, MTP modules and vision/audio towers. Equals params.counted_total minus params.counted_embedding. Same validation as params.counted_total.

params.counted_max_layer.label: Largest layer (counted)
params.counted_max_layer.definition: Largest group of language-backbone weights sharing a full layers.<index> tensor path, including every routed expert. Excludes lookup/Engram tables, embeddings, output head, MTP and other modalities. Hybrid checkpoints may store mixers and FFNs as separate layers. All-gather volume also depends on wrapping, sharding and dtype.

params.counted_active_non_embedding.label: Active non-emb. (counted)
params.counted_active_non_embedding.definition: Active parameters per token excluding the input embedding and output head, counted from the checkpoint as all non-expert weights plus routed-expert weights × top_k / experts. Same validation as params.counted_total.

params.note.label: Counting scope
params.note.definition: What the publisher's counts include or exclude (MTP modules, embeddings, vision encoder, n-gram tables).

params.embedding.label: Embedding params
params.embedding.definition: Parameters in input embedding and output head, as reported.

params.non_embedding.label: Non-embedding params
params.non_embedding.definition: Parameters excluding embedding and output head, as reported.

shape.layers.label: Layers
shape.layers.definition: Number of transformer blocks in the main backbone (attention or token mixer plus FFN), excluding MTP modules.

shape.vocab.label: Vocab
shape.vocab.definition: Embedding table rows (vocab_size in config, may include padding).

shape.tied_embeddings.label: Tied embeddings
shape.tied_embeddings.definition: Input embedding and output head share weights.

shape.memory.label: Lookup memory
shape.memory.definition: Hashed n-gram or conditional-memory tables outside the dense backbone (Engram, n-gram embeddings), with size and placement.

shape.tokenizer.label: Tokenizer
shape.tokenizer.definition: Tokenizer type and lineage as described by the publisher (e.g. byte-level BPE shared with an earlier model).

shape.aspect.label: d_model / layers
shape.aspect.definition: Width-to-depth ratio, d_model divided by the number of blocks.

attn.kind.label: Token mixers
attn.kind.definition: Token-mixing layer types in the backbone, e.g. GQA, MLA, SWA, Gated DeltaNet, Mamba-2, DSA (DeepSeek sparse attention).

attn.layout.label: Layer layout
attn.layout.definition: Token-mixer order, summarized as a pattern or layer positions. The fact's optional sequence lists each mixer in order; a ratio alone does not establish the order. Auxiliary prediction modules and standalone FFNs are excluded.

attn.global_layers.label: Global-attention layers
attn.global_layers.definition: Layers whose KV cache grows with full context (dense or sparse global attention, MLA). Excludes sliding-window and linear/recurrent layers.

attn.swa_ratio.label: SWA : global
attn.swa_ratio.definition: attn.local_layers divided by attn.global_layers, the sliding-window to global interleave ratio (5 for '5 SWA : 1 global').

attn.linear_ratio.label: Linear : global
attn.linear_ratio.definition: attn.linear_layers divided by attn.global_layers (3 for '3 Gated DeltaNet : 1 GQA').

attn.local_layers.label: Sliding-window layers
attn.local_layers.definition: Layers with a fixed attention window.

attn.linear_layers.label: Linear / SSM layers
attn.linear_layers.definition: Layers with a fixed-size recurrent state (linear attention, DeltaNet variants, Mamba).

attn.heads.label: Query heads
attn.heads.definition: Query heads in the global-attention layers.

attn.kv_heads.label: KV heads
attn.kv_heads.definition: Key/value heads in the global-attention layers. Not applicable to MLA, whose cache is a shared latent.

attn.qk_width.label: Heads × head dim
attn.qk_width.definition: attn.heads × attn.head_dim, the query projection width of global layers.

attn.group_size.label: Q heads / KV head
attn.group_size.definition: attn.heads divided by attn.kv_heads in global layers.

attn.head_dim.label: QK head dim
attn.head_dim.definition: Query/key dimension per head in global-attention layers (for MLA, nope + rope dims).

attn.v_head_dim.label: V head dim
attn.v_head_dim.definition: Value dimension per head in global layers (MLA v_head_dim; stated for MLA even when equal to the QK head dim).

attn.window.label: Window
attn.window.definition: Sliding-window size of the local layers.

attn.long_window_layers.label: Long-window SWA layers
attn.long_window_layers.definition: Sliding-window layers (counted in attn.local_layers) that use attn.long_window instead of attn.window.

attn.local_kv_heads.label: SWA KV heads
attn.local_kv_heads.definition: KV heads in sliding-window layers (stated even when equal to attn.kv_heads).

attn.local_heads.label: SWA query heads
attn.local_heads.definition: Query heads in sliding-window layers (stated even when equal to attn.heads).

attn.local_head_dim.label: SWA QK head dim
attn.local_head_dim.definition: Query/key head dimension in sliding-window layers. Value head dimensions may differ; see attn.local_v_head_dim.

attn.local_v_head_dim.label: SWA value head dim
attn.local_v_head_dim.definition: Value head dimension in sliding-window layers, when separately specified. KV formulas use this value when present, otherwise the explicit global value dimension, or the local QK dimension when no separate value dimension is given.

attn.kv_lora_rank.label: MLA KV latent
attn.kv_lora_rank.definition: Width of the compressed KV latent that MLA caches per token per layer.

attn.q_lora_rank.label: MLA Q latent
attn.q_lora_rank.definition: Width of the low-rank query projection in MLA; 0 when queries use a full-rank projection.

attn.rope_dim.label: Decoupled RoPE dim
attn.rope_dim.definition: Width of the shared positional key that MLA caches next to the latent.

attn.position.label: Positional encoding
attn.position.definition: Positional scheme in global layers: RoPE, partial RoPE, NoPE, or mixed per layer type.

attn.rope_theta.label: RoPE base
attn.rope_theta.definition: RoPE base frequency of the global layers at release.

attn.local_rope_theta.label: SWA RoPE base
attn.local_rope_theta.definition: RoPE base frequency of the sliding-window layers (stated even when equal to attn.rope_theta).

attn.rope_fraction.label: Rotary fraction
attn.rope_fraction.definition: Fraction of each head's QK dimensions that are rotated.

attn.qk_norm.label: QK norm
attn.qk_norm.definition: Queries and keys are normalized per head before the dot product.

attn.gate.label: Output gate
attn.gate.definition: Gate applied to the attention output before the output projection, with its placement.

attn.softcap.label: Attention logit softcap
attn.softcap.definition: tanh soft-capping value applied to attention logits.

attn.sparse.label: Sparse attention
attn.sparse.definition: Token-selection mechanism inside global layers, e.g. DSA lightning indexer with top-k.

attn.scale.label: Attention scaling
attn.scale.definition: Query-key scaling when it is not 1/sqrt(head_dim), e.g. query_pre_attn_scalar, length-dependent (SSMax-style) scaling, or value scaling.

attn.sinks.label: Attention sinks
attn.sinks.definition: Learned sink logits or sink bias in the softmax, with the layer types that use them.

attn.linear_kind.label: Linear-mixer details
attn.linear_kind.definition: Configuration of the linear / SSM layers (e.g. Gated DeltaNet heads and dims, Mamba-2 state size), as one string.

attn.linear_heads.label: Linear-mixer heads
attn.linear_heads.definition: Value heads (or SSM heads) in the linear / SSM layers.

attn.linear_head_dim.label: Linear-mixer head dim
attn.linear_head_dim.definition: Head dimension of the linear / SSM layers (value head dim for DeltaNet variants, head_dim for Mamba-2).

attn.indexer_dim.label: Indexer key dim
attn.indexer_dim.definition: Width of the sparse-attention indexer key cached per token in each global layer (DSA lightning indexer), counted in the KV cache.

attn.kv_sharing.label: Cross-layer KV sharing
attn.kv_sharing.definition: Layers that reuse another layer's KV cache instead of computing their own (YOCO-style, cross-layer attention), and which layers own caches.

attn.kv_groups.label: KV cache groups
attn.kv_groups.definition: Cache owners and entry shapes for compressed or shared attention. Each item specifies layers owning the cache, scalar elements per entry (K and V together), tokens_per_entry (compression ratio, default 1), and optionally window (maximum entries retained). Completed compressed entries are floor(context / tokens_per_entry); incomplete compressor state is excluded. KV sizes use these groups when present.

attn.kv_precision.label: KV storage formats
attn.kv_precision.definition: Sourced storage components of attn.kv_groups. Each component names its group and gives elements, bits per element, format, scale_count, scale_bits and padding_bytes per entry. Different parts of one entry can have different formats. Sourced-storage sizes are available only when every group's elements are covered. These are inference-cache formats; they do not establish pretraining precision.

attn.conv.label: Short conv kernel
attn.conv.definition: Kernel size of the causal short convolution in linear / SSM layers or attention projections.

ffn.dim.label: Dense FFN dim
ffn.dim.definition: Intermediate width of the dense FFN layers that are actually executed.

ffn.clamp.label: Activation clamp
ffn.clamp.definition: Clamping of GLU gate / up activations (e.g. SwiGLU limit 7), with the layers it applies to.

moe.expert_dim.label: Expert dim
moe.expert_dim.definition: Intermediate width of one routed expert.

moe.shared_dim.label: Shared expert dim
moe.shared_dim.definition: Total intermediate width of the shared expert(s).

moe.dense_layers.label: Leading dense layers
moe.dense_layers.definition: Number of initial blocks that use a dense FFN instead of MoE.

moe.router.label: Router score
moe.router.definition: Gating function over expert logits (softmax, sigmoid).

moe.balancing.label: Load balancing
moe.balancing.definition: Load-balancing method, with coefficients where disclosed.

moe.routed_scale.label: Routed scaling factor
moe.routed_scale.definition: Multiplier applied to the combined routed-expert output (routed_scaling_factor).

moe.norm_topk.label: Renormalize top-k
moe.norm_topk.definition: Selected expert weights are renormalized to sum to 1.

moe.groups.label: Group-limited routing
moe.groups.definition: Expert groups and groups selected per token, or node-limited routing, when used.

moe.latent_dim.label: Expert latent dim
moe.latent_dim.definition: Width of the projected space routed experts operate in (LatentMoE), when smaller than d_model.

moe.latent_ratio.label: Latent compression α (d_model / latent)
moe.latent_ratio.definition: shape.d_model divided by moe.latent_dim, how much LatentMoE compresses the hidden state before routed experts.

moe.sparsity.label: Sparsity (experts / top-k)
moe.sparsity.definition: Routed experts divided by experts selected per token.

mtp.depth.label: MTP depth
mtp.depth.definition: Additional future tokens predicted during pretraining (0 when the model was trained without MTP).

mtp.modules.label: MTP modules
mtp.modules.definition: MTP modules with distinct weights. 1 with mtp.depth > 1 means one module is applied recursively.

mtp.block.label: MTP module
mtp.block.definition: Contents of one MTP module (mixer and FFN type, norms, how the previous hidden state and next-token embedding are combined).

mtp.ffn.label: MTP FFN
mtp.ffn.definition: FFN in the MTP module: 'dense' or 'MoE', with its width when it differs from the backbone.

mtp.shares_embedding.label: MTP shares embedding/head
mtp.shares_embedding.definition: MTP modules use the main model's input embedding and output head.

mtp.params.label: MTP params
mtp.params.definition: Parameters of all MTP modules as reported by the publisher.

mtp.loss_weight.label: MTP loss weight
mtp.loss_weight.definition: Weight of the MTP loss, including its schedule.

mtp.released.label: MTP weights released
mtp.released.definition: The released checkpoint contains the MTP module weights.

norm.type.label: Norm
norm.type.definition: Normalization layer type in the blocks.

norm.placement.label: Norm placement
norm.placement.definition: Pre-norm, post-norm, or sandwich (pre and post).

norm.logit_softcap.label: Final logit softcap
norm.logit_softcap.definition: tanh soft-capping value on output logits.

norm.eps.label: Norm epsilon
norm.eps.definition: Epsilon of the block normalization layers.

norm.residual.label: Residual stream
norm.residual.definition: Residual design when it is not a plain sum, e.g. hyper-connections with n streams, gated residuals, depth-scaled residuals, FP32 residual accumulation.

norm.embedding.label: Embedding scaling
norm.embedding.definition: Scaling or normalization applied to input embeddings (e.g. × sqrt(d_model), RMSNorm after embedding).

norm.output_scale.label: Output logit scaling
norm.output_scale.definition: Scaling applied to output logits other than a softcap (e.g. muP-style width multiplier).

ctx.pretrain.label: Pretraining context
ctx.pretrain.definition: Sequence length of the main pretraining stage.

ctx.final.label: Trained context
ctx.final.definition: Longest sequence length trained on after context extension.

ctx.max.label: Advertised context
ctx.max.definition: Longest context the publisher says the model supports, possibly beyond trained length via RoPE scaling.

ctx.extension.label: Extension method
ctx.extension.definition: How context was extended (stages, RoPE base change, YaRN factor).

train.tokens.label: Pretraining tokens
train.tokens.definition: Tokens seen in pretraining including annealing and context extension, as reported.

train.optimizer.label: Optimizer
train.optimizer.definition: Optimizer used for the bulk of parameters.

train.lr_peak.label: Peak LR
train.lr_peak.definition: Peak learning rate of the main pretraining stage.

train.lr_min.label: Final LR
train.lr_min.definition: Learning rate at the end of the decay.

train.schedule.label: LR schedule
train.schedule.definition: Learning-rate schedule shape with phase boundaries.

train.warmup.label: Warmup
train.warmup.definition: Warmup length in steps or tokens.

train.batch.label: Batch schedule / notes
train.batch.definition: Global batch size, including any batch-size ramp: sequences × sequence length (token total), or the token total alone when only that is stated.

train.batch_tokens.label: Batch size (tokens)
train.batch_tokens.definition: Global batch size in tokens during the main pretraining stage, after any ramp (sequences × sequence length when stated in sequences, marked inferred).

train.betas.label: Adam betas
train.betas.definition: (beta1, beta2) of the Adam-family optimizer or its AdamW fallback.

train.dropout.label: Dropout
train.dropout.definition: Dropout rate applied during pretraining, with placement in the note. Recorded only when the publisher states it.

train.precision.label: Training precision
train.precision.definition: Matmul precision of pretraining (BF16, FP8 recipe, NVFP4 recipe) with the scaling granularity where disclosed. Never inferred from the released checkpoint dtype.

train.init.label: Initialization
train.init.definition: Weight initialization (std or scheme) as stated by the publisher; config initializer_range alone is not evidence.

train.stability.label: Stability measures
train.stability.definition: Interventions used during pretraining to keep it stable (QK-clip, z-loss, logit caps, spike handling), with coefficients.

train.masking.label: Document masking
train.masking.definition: Whether attention crosses document boundaries within a packed sequence.

train.objective.label: Extra objectives
train.objective.definition: Objectives beyond next-token prediction and MTP (fill-in-the-middle rate, distillation, multimodal tokens from the start).

train.data.label: Data mix
train.data.definition: Pretraining data composition as disclosed (domain shares, synthetic fraction, repetition).

train.hardware.label: Hardware
train.hardware.definition: Accelerators used for pretraining, count and duration where stated.

train.accelerators.label: Accelerators
train.accelerators.definition: Accelerator count and type for the main pretraining run, as the count with thousands separators and the chip's short name ("2,048 H800", "2,048 GH200"). A stated range or bound stays as stated ("2,048–4,096 GH200").

train.parallelism.label: Parallelism
train.parallelism.definition: Parallelism layout of the main pretraining run as stated, as degree-annotated terms in the order TP, PP, VPP, EP, CP, DP ("PP16 · EP64 · ZeRO-1 DP"); a term without a stated degree has none ("FSDP").

train.compute.label: Compute
train.compute.definition: Pretraining compute as stated (GPU-hours or FLOPs).

train.averaging.label: Checkpoint averaging
train.averaging.definition: EMA or checkpoint merging applied to produce the released base weights.

train.stages.label: Stages
train.stages.definition: Ordered pretraining stages. Each item: name, tokens, seq_len, lr, batch_tokens, batch_sequences, steps, note, quote, and source when it differs from the fact's source.

scaling.parametrization.label: Parametrization
scaling.parametrization.definition: Width/depth parametrization used to transfer hyperparameters: SP (standard), μP, CompleteP, u-μP, depth-μP, with the multipliers that differ from SP. Only when stated.

scaling.hp_rule.label: HP selection rule
scaling.hp_rule.definition: How peak LR, batch size or other hyperparameters were chosen for the released run (fitted scaling law with its formula, μP transfer from a proxy width, sweep), as stated.

scaling.ladder.label: Scaling ladder
scaling.ladder.definition: Smaller models trained to choose the architecture or recipe (sizes, token budgets), as disclosed.

scaling.tpp_active.label: Tokens / active param (non-embedding)
scaling.tpp_active.definition: train.tokens divided by params.counted_active_non_embedding, or by the stated params.active_non_embedding when there is no validated checkpoint count.

scaling.adamw_tau.label: AdamW timescale τ
scaling.adamw_tau.definition: B / (η λ D) with B = train.batch_tokens, η = train.lr_peak, λ = train.weight_decay and D = train.tokens: the AdamW EMA timescale as a fraction of training (Bergsma et al. 2025, Power Lines, arXiv 2505.13738). Computed only when the optimizer is AdamW; uses the peak LR.

kv.bytes_per_token.label: KV bytes / token
kv.bytes_per_token.definition: Retained KV cache divided by context length, including bounded SWA caches and indexer keys. Exports use uniform BF16 at 131,072 tokens. The website can select uniform payload precision (no quantization overhead) or sourced component formats (including scales and documented padding). This is cache payload, not peak prefill memory or persistent prefix storage.

kv.growth_per_token.label: Global KV bytes / token
kv.growth_per_token.definition: Long-context global KV bytes per token, including indexer keys; excludes bounded SWA caches. Compression rates and cross-layer cache reuse are included. Exports use uniform BF16; the website's storage selector also applies here. This is the field to compare with global-KV figures in reports, using the matching storage recipe.

kv.bytes_per_token_per_active.label: KV bytes / token / B active
kv.bytes_per_token_per_active.definition: kv.bytes_per_token divided by active parameters in billions (131,072 tokens in exports).

kv.bytes_at_context_per_active.label: KV at context / B active
kv.bytes_at_context_per_active.definition: kv.bytes_at_context divided by active parameters in billions (131,072 tokens in exports).

kv.bytes_at_context.label: KV at context
kv.bytes_at_context.definition: Retained KV cache for one sequence at the selected context, including SWA windows and indexer keys. Exports use uniform BF16 at 131,072 tokens. Excludes recurrent state, compressor tail state, draft/MTP caches, temporary prefill tensors, allocator metadata and persistent prefix snapshots. Does not estimate peak prefill or total serving memory.

eval.aa_index.label: AA Intelligence Index
eval.aa_index.definition: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 of the post-trained model, from a dated Wayback snapshot of its Artificial Analysis page. The note names the variant (reasoning setting).

eval.deepswe.label: DeepSWE pass@1
eval.deepswe.definition: DeepSWE v1.1 pass@1 (Datacurve; 113 tasks, same mini-swe-agent scaffold for every model), as a fraction.

meta.released.at: EPFL AI Center news, Apertus 1.5: Building the next generation of open AI infrastructure
meta.released.quote: Published 24 July, 2026 EPFL, ETH Zurich and the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) today released Apertus 1.5
meta.released.note: Release of the Apertus 1.5 suite on Hugging Face; the separate -base repository was created 2026-09-23 and the report is dated 2026-10-11.

meta.modality.quote: The models accept image and audio inputs in addition to text

params.total.quote: Apertus 1.5 is a family of 8B and 70B fully open, multilingual, and multimodal models
params.total.note: Size designation; no exact count is reported.

params.active.quote: Apertus 1.5 is a family of 8B and 70B fully open, multilingual, and multimodal models
params.active.note: Dense model; active equals the stated size.

params.note.value: 70B is a size designation; the checkpoint's 71,942,010,689 parameters include the image and audio tokenizers and the 266,752-row input embedding.
params.note.quote: "total_parameters": 71942010689

shape.vocab.note: Input embedding only: 131,072 text + 200 reserved + 131,072 image + 4,096 audio + 312 padding rows; the output head keeps the 131,072 text rows (/text_config/output_vocab_size).

shape.tokenizer.value: byte-level BPE (Mistral-Nemo tekken, 131,072) extended with 200 reserved slots, 131,072 image codes (Emu3.5 vision tokenizer, one per 16×16 patch) and 4,096 audio codes (WavTokenizer)
shape.tokenizer.quote: We extend the 131,072-entry vocabulary of Apertus 1.0 with 200 reserved multimodal slots, including structure markers, followed by 131,072 image codes
shape.tokenizer.note: Text tokenizer adapted from Mistral-Nemo-Base-2407 per the Apertus 1.0 report §2.2.

attn.kind.quote: such as grouped-query attention (GQA), RoPE, and RMSNorm

attn.layout.quote: Apertus 70B, with 80 layers and 64 parallel attention heads.

attn.head_dim.note: text_config has no head_dim, so hidden_size 8192 / 64 heads = 128.

attn.position.quote: following the LLaMA-3 implementation
attn.position.note: Released config: rope_type llama3, factor 32, low_freq_factor 1, high_freq_factor 4, original_max_position_embeddings 8192.

attn.rope_theta.note: 500,000 during Apertus 1.0 pretraining and Apertus 1.5 stages 1–3; 2M at 32K, 4M from 65K.

attn.qk_norm.note: Per-head RMSNorm on Q and K before RoPE; config qk_norm true, code builds the norms unconditionally.

ffn.activation.value: xIELU (non-gated; trainable α_p, α_n per layer)
ffn.activation.note: Config hidden_act xielu. xIELU(x) = α_p·x² + 0.5x for x > 0, α_n(eˣ − 1) − α_n·x + 0.5x otherwise (Apertus 1.0 report §2.1).

ctx.pretrain.quote: Both Apertus 8B and Apertus 70B were trained with a context of 4,096 tokens (about 3,000 words) during pretraining.

ctx.max.quote: handle contexts up to 262,144 tokens

ctx.extension.value: 8K → 32K → 65K → 131K → 262K after the stage-3 cooldown, 58.7B, 58.7B, 50.3B, 50.3B tokens; constant LR 2e-6, fresh optimizer per step; RoPE base 2M then 4M, Llama-3 scaling factor 8, 8, 16, 32; context parallelism 4, 8, 16, 32
ctx.extension.quote: The RoPE base grows to 2M for the first step and 4M thereafter, with scaling factors of 8, 8, 16, and 32.

shape.tokenizer.value: byte-level BPE, 163,840 tokens, inherited unchanged from A.X K1
shape.tokenizer.quote: The tokenizer is inherited unchanged from A.X K1: a byte-level BPE (Sennrich et al., 2016) vocabulary of 163,840 tokens

attn.gate.value: head-specific sigmoid gate on the attention output before o_proj, projected jointly with the query
attn.gate.note: Report p.3 §2.1: the gate is applied throughout pre-training.

attn.global_layers.quote: Of the 61 transformer layers, the first is a dense feed-forward layer and the remaining 60 are MoE layers
attn.global_layers.note: Every block uses MLA.

attn.kind.quote: The backbone uses Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) (Liu et al., 2024), which improves Key-Value cache efficiency
attn.kind.note: SGA = MLA plus the head-specific output gate and the top-k indexer (p.4 §2.2).

attn.layout.quote: Of the 61 transformer layers, the first is a dense feed-forward layer and the remaining 60 are MoE layers

attn.position.value: partial RoPE (64-dim decoupled RoPE key shared across heads, 128 NoPE dims per head)
attn.position.quote: q_rot, k_rot = apply_rotary_pos_emb_interleave(q_rot, k_rot, cos, sin)
attn.position.note: q_rot/k_rot are the /qk_rope_head_dim slices; the /qk_nope_head_dim slices are not rotated.

attn.q_lora_rank.note: q_gate_proj up-projects the normalized and raw query latents concatenated (2 × 1536 inputs) to per-head queries and gates.

attn.qk_norm.note: Report p.3 §2.1 says 'the query and key projections are normalized before the attention scores are computed (QK-normalization)', but the released code only RMS-normalizes the Q and KV latents (q_a_layernorm, kv_a_layernorm) before up-projection, as in DeepSeek-V3; per-head Q/K go to attention unnormalized.

attn.sparse.value: DSA-style indexer, top-2048 tokens per query; 64 indexer heads of dim 128, ReLU-scored
attn.sparse.quote: which uses a lightweight indexer to select a small set of top-k tokens (k = 2048) per query
attn.sparse.note: Indexer shape from config /index_n_heads 64, /index_head_dim 128, /index_topk 2048; scores pass through ReLU (AXK2Indexer.forward).

attn.indexer_dim.note: AXK2Indexer caches one key head: wk projects hidden_size to index_head_dim.

ffn.activation.note: act_fn is SiLU (/hidden_act).

moe.balancing.value: global auxiliary loss (4e-3 general and reasoning stages, 1e-3 long-context, 5e-4 SGA adaptation) plus a learnable expert bias (update rate 1e-3, lowered to 1e-4)
moe.balancing.quote: the (global, sequence-level) auxiliary-loss coefficients are set to (4 × 10−3 , off)
moe.balancing.note: Sequence-level term is monitored but not applied in the general and reasoning stages; it is switched on at 1e-5 for the long-context stages and 2e-5 for SGA adaptation.

moe.dense_layers.note: moe_layer_freq 1: every later layer is MoE.

moe.groups.value: 256 experts in 8 groups, top-4 groups per token
moe.groups.quote: the 256 routed experts are partitioned into 8 groups, and each token activates the top 8 experts under a group top-k of 4

moe.shared_dim.note: 1 shared expert (/n_shared_experts) of the routed-expert width.

mtp.released.note: No MTP, nextn or layers.61 tensors in the weight map; /num_nextn_predict_layers is 0; the report does not mention MTP.

norm.type.note: Gated Norm: each block RMSNorm except the dense layer 0's pre-FFN norm is followed by an input-dependent sigmoid gate from a rank-16 SiLU MLP (/gated_norm_rank).

ctx.pretrain.quote: A.X K2 is trained on a corpus of 6.4 trillion tokens at a sequence length of 4,096

train.batch.quote: linearly increasing the batch size from 2,048 to 16,384 in increments of 2,048 over the first 72 million sequences (approximately 295B tokens at a sequence length of 4,096)

train.batch_tokens.quote: the global batch size to 16,384 sequences (with a micro-batch size of 4), corresponding to approximately 64M tokens per step at a sequence length of 4,096

meta.released.note: Post: 'Today, we have released Beam’s model weights on Hugging Face'; the Oct 5 announcement preceded the weights.

meta.modality.quote: Beam takes text as input and generates text as output.

params.total.quote: Total Parameters 501.3B

params.active.quote: Active Parameters 23.4B

attn.kind.quote: Gated GQA + Sliding Window Attention

attn.layout.note: /layer_types has full_attention at layers 5, 11, ..., 47 and 51; all others sliding_attention. Ordered 52-layer backbone from /layer_types; auxiliary modules are excluded.

attn.kv_heads.note: Same count on SWA and global layers (BeamAttention).

attn.local_heads.note: BeamAttention builds q/k/v from the same num_attention_heads, num_key_value_heads and head_dim for both layer types; only sliding_window differs.

attn.position.quote: # Sliding-attention layers use RoPE; full-attention layers use NoPE with position-dependent query scaling.
attn.position.note: Config /rope_parameters: sliding_attention rope_theta 10000.0, full_attention null.

attn.scale.value: 1/sqrt(head_dim); global (NoPE) layers also scale q by (1 + n/2048)^0.1 at 1-based position n (SSMax-style)
attn.scale.quote: Scalable-softmax query scale, `(1 + position / 2048) ** 0.1`, for layers that run without RoPE.
attn.scale.note: Code computes exp(0.1 · log1p((position_ids + 1) / 2048)) with 0-based position_ids; SWA layers are unscaled.

attn.gate.value: elementwise sigmoid gate, gate_proj of the normed attention input plus a per-head bias, before o_proj

ffn.activation.quote: # Beam evaluates the SwiGLU activation and product in FP32.
ffn.activation.note: act_fn is config /hidden_act silu; routed experts use the same gate × up form (BeamExperts._apply_gate).

ffn.bias.note: Routed experts hold only gate_up_proj and down_proj weights (BeamExperts).

moe.dense_layers.note: Card: 52: 3 dense + 49 MoE.

moe.shared.note: BeamMoE holds only the router and routed experts; no shared-expert module.

moe.groups.value: 8 groups, top-4 groups per token (group score = sum of top-2 biased scores)

moe.balancing.value: auxiliary-loss-free bias with cosine-decayed bias updates, plus sequence-level balancing
moe.balancing.at: Pretraining a Foundation for Reasoning; Stable and balanced MoE optimization
moe.balancing.quote: introducing cosine decay of expert-bias updates to reduce routing perturbations later in training
moe.balancing.note: Also: 'Sequence-level balancing further encourages balanced expert utilization'. Coefficients not disclosed.

norm.placement.at: Pretraining a Foundation for Reasoning; Stable and balanced MoE optimization
norm.placement.quote: Combined with SandwichNorm, elementwise attention gating, and FP32 residual accumulation
norm.placement.note: Post-norms apply before the depth-scaled residual add.

norm.residual.value: depth-scaled sum r·sqrt((k-1)/k) + h/sqrt(k), k = 2(i+1) for attention and 2(i+1)+1 for FFN in 0-indexed layer i; FP32 residual accumulation
norm.residual.at: Pretraining a Foundation for Reasoning; Stable and balanced MoE optimization
norm.residual.quote: we developed a depth-based scaling approach that counteracts activation growth as sublayer outputs accumulate, helping keep residual norms stable as model depth increases. Combined with SandwichNorm, elementwise attention gating, and FP32 residual accumulation
norm.residual.note: Formula from modeling_beam.py depth_scaled_residual_add and BeamDecoderLayer.__init__.

ctx.extension.value: extended to 1M during midtraining

attn.kind.quote: we introduce a hybrid architecture combining sparse and linear attention
attn.kind.note: Linear layers are Kimi Delta Attention (Glm5NextTextLinearAttention); sparse layers are MLA with a DSA indexer (Glm5NextTextAttention).

attn.layout.note: 0-indexed MLA+DSA layers of 45; the rest (kda_layers), including the last (44), are KDA. Ordered 45-layer backbone from /text_config/layer_types; auxiliary modules are excluded.

attn.head_dim.note: 256 nope + 0 rope. The config's /text_config/head_dim=0 is the RoPE sub-dim.

attn.qk_norm.note: MLA layers normalize only the Q and KV latents; KDA layers L2-normalize q/k inside the recurrence.

attn.indexer_dim.note: One key head; IndexPool pools 4 consecutive keys into one (see attn.kv_groups).

value.name: MLA latent
value.note: kv_lora_rank 512, no RoPE key.

value.name: IndexPool indexer key
value.note: Blog: IndexPool compresses four indexer key vectors into one; transformers caches unpooled keys and pools at scoring time.

params.note.quote: activated_value_params = self.model_dim * self.num_kv_heads * self.head_dim * self.num_activated_values
params.note.note: Per MoVA+MoE layer: 34.1M Q/K/O/gate + 64 × 2.62M value experts (4 active) + 100 × 5.9M routed experts (8 active) + 5.9M shared + routers; × 45 layers, plus 3 dense layers of 83.9M.

attn.kind.value: GQA (MoVA: routed value projections in 45 of 48 layers)
attn.kind.quote: MoVA attention with routed value experts and optional post-attention gate.
attn.kind.note: MoVA (Mixture-of-Value Attention) replaces v_proj with 64 value experts (/mova_num_experts), each a 2560→8×128 linear map; a sigmoid router picks 4 per token (/mova_num_experts_per_tok), and the SiLU'd expert outputs are summed with renormalized weights × 2.5. Q and K are ordinary GQA, every token attends to all earlier tokens, and the mixed V is cached like a normal V, so the KV cache is the standard 8 × (128 + 128) per layer. sliding_window null, use_sliding_window false.

attn.layout.value: 3 GQA, then 45 GQA with MoVA values
attn.layout.note: MoVA layers are exactly the MoE-FFN layers; layers 0-2 (/mlp_only_layers) use a plain v_proj and a dense FFN.

attn.position.quote: "rope_head_dim": 128
attn.position.note: rope_head_dim equals head_dim, so all 128 QK dims rotate (unlike the 375B sibling's 64).

attn.gate.value: softplus (β = ln 2) gate per head dimension on the attention output, before o_proj, in all layers
attn.gate.note: Gate is gate_proj(x), 2560 → 32 × 128, selected by /attention_gate_func.

ffn.activation.note: act_fn is SiLU (/hidden_act); dense FFN, routed and shared experts all use K2HorizonMLP.

moe.dense_layers.note: Layers 0, 1, 2 use the 6144-wide dense FFN; decoder_sparse_step 1 makes every later layer MoE.

attn.indexer_dim.note: One index key head shared across KV groups (MiniMaxM3VLIndexer.k_proj outputs index_head_dim); 4 index query heads (sparse_num_index_heads); cached only in the 57 MSA layers.

ffn.activation.note: Config hidden_act = swigluoai, swiglu_alpha = 1.702; output (up + 1.0) * glu; inputs clamped (see ffn.clamp).

ffn.clamp.value: gate clamped at max 7, up clamped to [−7, 7] before the GLU; all dense, shared and routed FFNs

moe.routed_scale.note: Multiplies the routed-expert output before the shared expert is added (MiniMaxM3VLSparseMoeBlock.forward).

mtp.released.note: Config declares num_mtp_modules=7 and num_nextn_predict_layers=1; the checkpoint has no mtp.* tensors.

meta.modality.note: No modality statement; text-generation pipeline tag and a causal LM config with no vision or audio config.

params.total.quote: We introduce Motif 3, a decoder-only Mixture-of-Experts language model with 314 billion total parameters and 13.2 billion parameters activated for each token.

params.active.quote: We introduce Motif 3, a decoder-only Mixture-of-Experts language model with 314 billion total parameters and 13.2 billion parameters activated for each token.

shape.tokenizer.value: SuperBPE trained from scratch (stage 2 adds multi-word superword tokens), 220,160 vocab
shape.tokenizer.quote: We trained the Motif 3 tokenizer from scratch using the SuperBPE reference implementation

attn.kind.value: GDLA (MLA latent KV + grouped differential attention), SWA
attn.kind.quote: Motif 3 is built around Grouped Differential Latent Attention (GDLA), which integrates grouped differential attention with the compressed key-value representation of Multi-head Latent Attention.

attn.layout.quote: Under zero-based indexing, layers 0, 4, 8, . . . use full attention, while the three intervening layers use sliding-window attention.
attn.layout.note: Both layer types use GDLA; config use_sliding_window true, sliding_window_pattern interleave. The source gives zero-based order explicitly; modeling_motif.py uses layer_idx % sliding_window_period, with config period 4.

attn.global_layers.note: Config has no per-layer list; with /sliding_window_period 4 and /num_hidden_layers 53, layers 0, 4, …, 52 are full attention.

attn.window.quote: the remaining layers use sliding-window attention with a window of 128 tokens.
attn.window.note: config sliding_window 128; HF code passes sliding_window + 1 to flash attention.

attn.heads.quote: GDLA uses 80 query heads and 16 KV heads
attn.heads.note: num_attention_heads 80, num_key_value_heads 16. All 80 heads (64 signal + 16 noise, g = 4) compute attention; each group of 4 signal + 1 noise heads shares one of 16 KV heads up-projected from the latent. Each noise output is subtracted from its group's signal outputs, so W_O sees 64 heads × 128.

attn.head_dim.quote: with a query-key head dimension of 192, a value-head dimension of 128, and a 64-dimensional rotary component.

attn.v_head_dim.quote: with a query-key head dimension of 192, a value-head dimension of 128, and a 64-dimensional rotary component.

attn.kv_lora_rank.quote: The query and KV low-rank dimensions are 1,024 and 512, respectively.

attn.q_lora_rank.quote: The query and KV low-rank dimensions are 1,024 and 512, respectively.

attn.rope_dim.quote: with a query-key head dimension of 192, a value-head dimension of 128, and a 64-dimensional rotary component.

attn.position.value: partial RoPE (decoupled 64-dim RoPE key shared across heads + 128 NoPE dims); YaRN on global layers only
attn.position.at: p.19 §4.3 Batch size and context-length schedule
attn.position.quote: The full-attention layers use a DeepSeek-YaRN extension from the original 4K context length to 256K, with an extension factor of 64, while the sliding-window layers retain local RoPE without long-range extension.

attn.local_heads.note: MotifGDLAttention reads the same head counts and dims for SWA and full layers; only the window and rotary embedding differ.

attn.local_head_dim.note: QK 192, V 128 (/v_head_dim), as in global layers.

attn.local_rope_theta.note: SWA layers build their own rotary embedding with rope_scaling None (no YaRN).

attn.qk_norm.note: RMSNorm is applied only to the Q and KV latents before up-projection, not per head.

attn.gate.value: element-wise sigmoid gate from the normalized query latent, on the differential output before W_O
attn.gate.quote: Before the final output projection, the differential representation is modulated by an element-wise sigmoid gate computed from the normalized query latent
attn.gate.note: config elementwise_attn_output_gate true; diff_v2 true selects the input-dependent λ variant (the only one in HF code).

attn.scale.note: /rope_factor 64, /mscale 1. Differential output: attn1 - sigmoid(lambda_proj(x)) * attn2, λ per token and signal head (report Eq. 12–13).

attn.bias.note: wq_b, wkv_a, wkv_b, lambda_proj and wo are also bias=False.

ffn.activation.value: Expert-Specific PolyNorm (gated: PolyNorm(gate) × up; per-expert sigmoid-bounded coefficients)
ffn.activation.quote: Motif 3 instead replaces the SiLU gate activation with Expert-Specific PolyNorm, whose polynomial coefficients and bias are learned independently for each expert.
ffn.activation.note: config hidden_act poly_norm. PolyNorm(z) = Σ_{n=1..3} a_n·z^n/RMS(z^n) + b; dense layers and the shared expert use a single PolyNorm. Code multiplies the activation output by /polynorm_output_scale 0.5.

ffn.clamp.quote: We avoid this forward-pass intervention because activation outliers are not necessarily meaningless numerical artifacts.
ffn.clamp.note: Routed-expert PolyNorm bias is clipped to [-0.5, 0.5] (Eq. 24, /polynorm_bias_clamp); the HF code's ±1e6 /hidden_clamp is a numerical guard.

ffn.dim.quote: The first two layers use dense feed-forward networks with an intermediate dimension of 12,288

ffn.bias.note: Up and down projections also bias=False; the PolyNorm activation itself has a learned scalar bias.

moe.experts.quote: Each MoE layer contains 384 routed experts and one shared expert.

moe.top_k.quote: The router uses normalized sigmoid scores and selects eight routed experts per token.

moe.shared.quote: Each MoE layer contains 384 routed experts and one shared expert.

moe.expert_dim.quote: Each routed expert has an intermediate dimension of 1,280.

moe.shared_dim.note: 1 shared expert (/num_shared_experts) of the routed-expert width (MoE.__init__).

moe.dense_layers.quote: The first two layers use dense feed-forward networks with an intermediate dimension of 12,288, while the remaining 51 layers use sparse MoE feed-forward networks.
moe.dense_layers.note: config n_dense_first_layers 2, interleave_moe_layer_step 1.

moe.router.quote: The router uses normalized sigmoid scores and selects eight routed experts per token.
moe.router.note: Routing computed in FP32; config score_func sigmoid, route_norm true.

moe.balancing.value: aux-loss-free bias (coefficient 1e-3) + sequence-wise aux loss 1e-4 (2.4e-4 layer 2, 2.0e-4 layers 3–5) + cosine-decayed Gaussian router-logit noise
moe.balancing.quote: The sequence-wise auxiliary load-balancing loss is summed over tokens and uses a default weight of 1 × 10−4 . We increase this weight to 2.4 × 10−4 for layer 2 and to 2.0 × 10−4 for layers 3–5.
moe.balancing.note: Bias coefficient 1 × 10−3 in the same paragraph; router noise in §4.2. Collapsed routers were replaced with an adjacent layer's router and biases.

mtp.depth.quote: MTP head 1 layer for self-speculative decoding
mtp.depth.note: One DeepSeek-V3-style MTP module (§2.5); the index holds only mtp_layers.0.

mtp.modules.note: Only mtp_layers.0 in the index; training code builds one module (multi_token_preds=1).

mtp.block.value: concat(h, RMSNorm(next-token embedding)) → linear 2d→d → GDLA block (SWA, no mHC) with dense PolyNorm FFN → RMSNorm → shared output head
mtp.block.note: Code comment: 'Force dense FFN, SWA, and no MHC for MTP blocks'.

mtp.ffn.quote: interleave_moe_layer_step=0: always use dense FeedForward (no MoE)
mtp.ffn.note: Dense FFN width is intermediate_dim 12288; index has mlp.gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj, no experts.

mtp.shares_embedding.note: The next-token embedding is the main tok_embeddings output (raw_embeds in Motif.forward).

mtp.loss_weight.quote: The MTP auxiliary objective uses a loss weight of 0.2.
mtp.loss_weight.note: Training code multiplies by mtp_depth_decay 0.95 and divides the summed loss by 1 + weight.

mtp.released.note: The card says the MTP head is not shipped, but shard model-00104-of-00155 contains mtp_layers.0 (GDLA + dense PolyNorm FFN, 19 tensors); the HF modeling code does not load it.

norm.type.quote: We apply RMSNorm [74] before each sublayer

norm.placement.quote: We apply RMSNorm [74] before each sublayer and use modified manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC) [68] in place of conventional residual additions.

norm.residual.value: modified mHC: 4 streams, Sinkhorn-Knopp doubly stochastic residual mixing, post-mapping multiplier annealed 2 → 1 during pretraining
norm.residual.quote: We use an expansion rate of n = 4, corresponding to four parallel residual streams.
norm.residual.note: config mhc_enabled true, mhc_expansion_rate 4. Mappings computed in FP32 from an RMSNorm of the flattened streams; 20 Sinkhorn iterations (/mhc_sinkhorn_iters); embedding copied to all 4 streams and streams averaged before the final norm (MotifModel.forward).

ctx.pretrain.at: p.19 §4.3 Batch size and context-length schedule
ctx.pretrain.quote: Pretraining begins with sequences of up to 4K tokens.

ctx.final.quote: Context Length 262,144 (256K)
ctx.final.note: Report §4.3: a dedicated long-context stage with sequences of up to 256K tokens.

ctx.max.quote: Native 256K context (262,144 tokens), trained with window-aware context parallelism.

ctx.extension.value: 4K → 32K during the LR decay phase → 256K stage; DeepSeek-YaRN factor 64 on global layers only
ctx.extension.at: p.19 §4.3 Batch size and context-length schedule
ctx.extension.quote: During the learning-rate decay phase, we transition to a maximum sequence length of 32K tokens, followed by a dedicated long-context stage with sequences of up to 256K tokens.
ctx.extension.note: Config rope_scaling: rope_type yarn, factor 64, original_max_position_embeddings 4096 (original_seq_len), beta_fast 32, beta_slow 1, theta 10000.

train.tokens.quote: Motif 3 is pretrained on approximately 12.5 trillion tokens, measured with the Motif tokenizer

train.optimizer.value: Muon + AdamW (AdamW for embeddings, output head and vector parameters)
train.optimizer.quote: Embeddings, the output projection, and vector-shaped parameters are instead optimized with AdamW.
train.optimizer.note: Each routed expert is orthogonalized as its own matrix; Newton–Schulz in BF16.

train.lr_peak.quote: Training starts with a learning rate of 3 × 10−4 and follows a warmup-stable-decay (WSD) learning-rate schedule.

train.lr_min.quote: The subsequent 256K long-context stage continues from this checkpoint and further reduces the learning rate to 3 × 10−5 .

train.schedule.value: WSD: stable at 3e-4, decay to 7.5e-5 during the 4K → 32K transition, then 256K stage decays to 3e-5
train.schedule.quote: The stable phase performs the majority of pretraining at the maximum learning rate, after which the decay phase reduces the learning rate to 7.5 × 10−5 while transitioning from 4K to 32K sequences.

train.batch.value: up to 75M tokens
train.batch.at: p.19 §4.3 Batch size and context-length schedule
train.batch.quote: The global training batch contains up to 75 million tokens.

train.batch_tokens.at: p.19 §4.3 Batch size and context-length schedule
train.batch_tokens.quote: The global training batch contains up to 75 million tokens.
train.batch_tokens.note: Stated as an upper bound; no ramp described.

train.precision.value: MXFP8 for MoE expert grouped GEMMs and EP dispatch; BF16 elsewhere; FP32 master weights, gradients, router logits and Muon states; BF16 gradient communication with FP32 reduction
train.precision.quote: More specifically, we apply MXFP8 [59] to the MoE experts

train.stability.value: QK-Clip (τ=100, 200 in the 256K stage; every 10 steps; key-side share 1/(1+√G)); FFN-output magnitude penalty (weight 2e-4, threshold 128, 1,024 on the final layer); mHC post-multiplier annealing; FP32 routing; router replacement on collapse
train.stability.quote: We perform monitoring and clipping every 10 steps, using τ = 100 during main pre-training and τ = 200 during the 256K-token long-context stage.
train.stability.note: Penalty values: 'The FFN magnitude regularizer uses a loss weight of 2.0 × 10−4 and a threshold of 128' (p.19).

train.masking.quote: Document-masked packing concatenates multiple documents into a fixed-length sequence while preventing cross-document attention.
train.masking.note: Stated in the long-context training section; not stated separately for the 4K stage.

train.data.value: ~70% NVIDIA Nemotron pretraining collection (some components filtered), most of the rest in-house web, STEM and synthetic; dedicated Korean, multilingual, legal and financial data; dynamic mixture 19 → 57 datasets; reasoning data <5%
train.data.quote: The retained Nemotron data account for approximately 70% of the full Motif 3 pretraining corpus.
train.data.note: Long-context stage uses ~5% of the corpus reconstructed as long-context data (§4.3).

train.cutoff.quote: The latest data included in the corpus were collected through March 2026, which we use as the model’s knowledge cutoff.

train.accelerators.quote: With expert and parameter sharding, optimizer-state CPU offloading, and the memory capacity of B200 GPUs

train.parallelism.quote: Outside the expert-parallel dimension, we use a sharded data-parallel (DP-shard) degree of 8 and assign the remaining ranks to the replicated data-parallel (DP-replicate) dimension.
train.parallelism.note: Same paragraph: EP = 8 within one eight-GPU node, FSDP sharding, no pipeline parallelism.

attn.local_heads.quote: Number of Attention Heads: 128 for Q and 16 for KV (grouped-query attention)
attn.local_heads.note: One attention class for both layer types; only the window and RoPE differ (MuseSparkTextAttention, torchtitan _muse_spark_config).

attn.local_kv_heads.quote: Number of Attention Heads: 128 for Q and 16 for KV (grouped-query attention)

attn.local_head_dim.note: Same attention class on SWA and global layers.

attn.local_rope_theta.note: Also the rope_parameters default of MuseSparkTextConfig; global layers are NoPE.

attn.window.note: MuseSparkTextConfig default; the class is declared for this checkpoint (auto_docstring checkpoint=meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B).

attn.position.quote: Defaults to the global theta everywhere except every 4th layer counted backward from the last, which is NoPE.

attn.qk_norm.note: Weightless RMSNorm on Q and K (MuseSparkTextAttention); see attn.scale.

attn.scale.note: MuseSparkTextConfig default; the class is declared for this checkpoint (auto_docstring checkpoint=meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B). Applied in MuseSparkTextAttention.forward.

attn.bias.note: MuseSparkTextConfig default; the class is declared for this checkpoint (auto_docstring checkpoint=meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B).

attn.gate.value: elementwise sigmoid gate computed from the block input, applied after a weightless per-head output RMSNorm, before o_proj
attn.gate.note: Card: output gate and output norm on the attention block.

ffn.activation.note: act_fn is hidden_act, silu by MuseSparkTextConfig default (class declared for this checkpoint).

ffn.clamp.note: The torchtitan 816B-A42B flavor also uses plain SwiGLU; only torchtitan's Dist-MoE throughput recipes for continued training from the released checkpoint swap in ClampedSwiGLU (limit 7, α 1.702, up + 1), a different function, so it does not describe pretraining.

ffn.bias.note: Experts hold only gate_up_proj and down_proj weights; no bias parameters.

moe.expert_dim.note: MuseSparkTextConfig default; the class is declared for this checkpoint (auto_docstring checkpoint=meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B). Experts run at moe_hidden_size 4096 (see moe.latent_dim).

moe.shared.quote: self.experts = MuseSparkExperts(config) self.post_expert_proj = nn.Linear(config.moe_hidden_size, config.hidden_size, bias=False)
moe.shared.note: MuseSparkMoE has a router, pre/post projections and routed experts only; no shared-expert branch.

moe.dense_layers.note: MuseSparkTextConfig default; the torchtitan 816B-A42B flavor also builds a MoE FFN in all 62 layers.

moe.router.note: Logits computed in FP32 and scaled by output_multiplier; an e_score_correction_bias buffer is added for top-k selection only.

moe.routed_scale.note: MuseSparkTextConfig default; the class is declared for this checkpoint (auto_docstring checkpoint=meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B).

moe.latent_dim.note: MuseSparkTextConfig default; the class is declared for this checkpoint (auto_docstring checkpoint=meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B). pre_expert_proj 8192 → 4096 (then RMSNorm) before the experts, post_expert_proj back to 8192.

norm.type.note: Pre-attention and pre-FFN norms; post-attention norm is weightless, post-FFN norm scales the input by (1+w) before normalizing, final norm is a plain RMSNorm.

norm.placement.note: The post-norm output joins the residual through a learned gate (see norm.residual).

norm.eps.note: MuseSparkTextConfig default; the class is declared for this checkpoint (auto_docstring checkpoint=meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B). Post-attention, post-FFN and post-expert norms use post_norm_eps 1e-8.

norm.residual.value: learned per-channel residual gate: alpha·residual + beta·h, beta = sigmoid(g/0.3), alpha = sqrt(sigmoid(-g/0.3)·(1+beta))
norm.residual.note: Temperature 0.3 is the residual_gate_temperature default of MuseSparkTextConfig (class declared for this checkpoint).

norm.output_scale.quote: Equal to `1/sqrt(hidden_size / 256)` for the released checkpoint.
norm.output_scale.note: Router logits are scaled by the same output_multiplier.

norm.logit_softcap.note: MuseSparkTextConfig default; the class is declared for this checkpoint (auto_docstring checkpoint=meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B). Logits are first multiplied by output_multiplier (see norm.output_scale).

attn.gate.value: sigmoid, elementwise on the attention output before o_proj; gate projected jointly with Q

attn.kind.at: README.md; Highlights; Hybrid Attention with QSA

params.active.quote: Solar Open 2 is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Transformer with 250B total parameters and 15B active parameters per token.

shape.tokenizer.value: byte-level BPE, 196,608 vocab, digit splitting; inherited unchanged from Solar Open 1
shape.tokenizer.quote: It is a custom byte-level BPE tokenizer with a 196,608-token vocabulary, trained on a corpus that oversamples Korean and the target domains, with digit splitting and whitespace preservation for arithmetic and code fidelity.

attn.kind.quote: It adopts GQA (Ainslie et al., 2023) for the softmax layers and KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) (Yang et al., 2025; Kimi Team, 2025) for the linear layers

attn.layout.value: 3 KDA : 1 GQA (GQA first in each block of 4)
attn.layout.note: Config /gqa_layers puts GQA at layers 0, 4, …, 44 (gqa_interval 3 KDA layers between). /gqa_layers gives zero-based global-attention indices; other layers use KDA.

attn.linear_layers.quote: so that 12 of the 48 layers (25%) are softmax and 36 (75%) are linear

attn.position.quote: Solar Open 2 removes positional encoding entirely
attn.position.note: Config /use_rope is false, so SolarOpen2Attention skips RoPE and /rope_theta is unused; KDA layers carry token order.

attn.qk_norm.note: GQA layers have no q/k norm weights; KDA layers L2-normalize q and k inside the kernel.

attn.gate.value: elementwise sigmoid gate on SDPA output (g_proj from layer input), GQA layers
attn.gate.note: Config use_gqa_gate true. KDA layers use a sigmoid-gated RMSNorm on their output (SolarOpen2RMSNormGated).

attn.linear_kind.value: KDA with negative eigenvalues (β = 2σ(·) ∈ (0, 2)); 64 heads × 128, no KV grouping; short conv 4 on q/k/v; low-rank (rank 128) decay and output-gate projections
attn.linear_kind.quote: Solar Open 2 instead sets allow_neg_eigval=True: widening the write strength to β = 2σ(·) ∈ (0, 2)
attn.linear_kind.note: Config kda_allow_neg_eigval true. Heads, dims and conv from config /linear_attn_config; low-rank gates from /kda_use_full_proj false (f_a_proj/g_a_proj project to head_dim).

ffn.activation.note: act_fn is SiLU (report Table 1); the shared expert uses the same gate × up form (SolarOpen2MLP).

moe.router.note: Expert selection adds a per-expert e_score_correction_bias (present in the weights); the report does not describe the balancing method.

norm.placement.quote: a single shared expert with no dense layers, and pre-norm residuals.

ctx.final.quote: augments it with long-document data including repo-level code, and extends training to a 1M context length.

ctx.extension.value: Stage 4 Length Expansion (865B tokens): continued training to 1M on a higher-quality corpus plus long documents and repo-level code; NoPE
ctx.extension.quote: Length Expansion closes pre-training with 0.9T tokens of continued training that extend the context window to 1M and inject reasoning and agent data.

train.tokens.quote: Stages 2–4 then train on about 12T tokens in total
train.tokens.note: Stages sum to 11.865T (10T + 1T + 865B, Figure 8); excludes Solar Open 1 training behind the 5.69B transferred weights.

train.init.value: selective weight transfer from Solar Open 1: 5.69B params (2.3%) transferred (embedding/output, norms, GQA q/k/v/o, shared expert; KDA q/o re-mapped from GQA q/o); routed experts, router, KDA k/v, decay/write gates, conv and GQA output gate randomly initialized

train.averaging.quote: To compensate, we selected four intermediate checkpoints and merged them, obtaining a pre-trained language model (PLM) stronger than any single checkpoint.
train.averaging.note: The merged PLM is the post-training starting point and is not released; merge weights are not stated.

meta.modality.quote: Step3p5ForCausalLM
meta.modality.note: Causal-LM class with no vision config.

params.total.quote: This configuration maintains an extensive knowledge capacity (196B total parameters)

params.active.quote: restricting per-token activation to just 11B

params.active_non_embedding.note: Table 6 states activated params exclude embedding/output matrices; backbone without the 3 MTP heads.

params.note.value: Backbone only: 198B total / 13B active with the 3 MTP heads; active count excludes embedding and output matrices.
params.note.quote: “Activated params” are reported per token and exclude embedding/output matrices.

attn.kind.quote: This configuration repeats a four-layer motif consisting of three SWA layers (W =512) followed by a single full GQA-8 layer.

attn.layout.value: 3 SWA : 1 global (leading global layer + 11 × [3 SWA, 1 global])
attn.layout.note: Ordered 45-layer backbone from /layer_types; auxiliary modules are excluded. The array has 46 entries; only the first num_hidden_layers=45 are backbone layers.

attn.global_layers.note: /layer_types has 46 entries; the last is the MTP layer.

attn.local_heads.note: Step3p5Attention.__init__ reads it for sliding_attention layers.

attn.local_kv_heads.note: Step3p5Attention.__init__ reads it for sliding_attention layers.

attn.local_head_dim.note: Step3p5Attention uses config head_dim for both layer types; /attention_other_setting/head_dim (128) is not read.

attn.kv_heads.note: Step3p5Attention reads num_attention_groups as the KV head count.

attn.position.value: partial RoPE (global, 64 of 128 dims), RoPE (SWA, all 128 dims)
attn.position.quote: RoPE dims (full / SWA) 64 / 128

attn.local_rope_theta.note: Per-layer list read by Step3p5RotaryEmbedding; 10,000 on every sliding_attention layer.

attn.rope_fraction.note: Global layers; SWA layers use 1.0. Step3p5RotaryEmbedding reads the per-layer factor.

attn.rope_theta.note: Global layers; SWA layers 10,000. 10,000 for all layers at 4K, raised to 1M for full attention in the 32K portion of annealing (p.15 §4.2.3).

attn.qk_norm.note: Per-head zero-centered RMSNorm on Q and K, before RoPE; applied regardless of /use_qk_norm.

attn.gate.value: head-wise scalar sigmoid gate on each head's output, before o_proj; all layers
attn.gate.note: Enabled by /use_head_wise_attn_gate; g_proj maps hidden_size → num_heads; paper App. A.1. Used instead of attention sinks (/sink false).

ffn.activation.note: gate = SiLU(gate_proj(x)); routed experts use the same form (Step3p5MoEMLP.get_expert_output).

ffn.clamp.value: gate capped at 7, up clamped to [−7, 7] in routed experts of layers 43–44; shared expert of layer 44 limit 16
ffn.clamp.note: Limits from /swiglu_limits and /swiglu_limits_shared (0-indexed, 0 = no clamp); paper §4.1.3 adopts activation clipping in deep MoE layers against expert activation blow-up.

moe.shared.quote: Each MoE layer contains 288 routed experts plus one shared expert

moe.dense_layers.quote: Step 3.5 Flash adopts a 45-layer sparse-MoE Transformer backbone (3 dense layers and 42 MoE layers)
moe.dense_layers.note: Config moe_layers_enum lists layers 3–44.

moe.router.note: Bias (use_moe_router_bias) added for top-k selection only; moe_router_activation sigmoid; router logits computed in FP32 (/need_fp32_gate).

moe.norm_topk.note: Hard-coded in code; config norm_expert_weight true agrees.

moe.routed_scale.note: Applied to routed weights in Step3p5MoEMLP.forward; paper §4.1.2 motivates an explicit routed/shared scale against expert collapse.

moe.balancing.value: aux-loss-free bias (update rate 0.001 for the first 14.6T, decayed to 0 during annealing) + EP-group balance loss 0.001
moe.balancing.quote: the bias update rate is 0.001 for the first 14.6T tokens and decays to 0.0 during annealing, and an EP-group balance loss with coefficient 0.001 is applied throughout pre-training.
moe.balancing.note: EP-group loss balances load across expert-parallel rank groups (Eq. 1, §2.2).

mtp.depth.quote: we activate and optimize only MTP-1 in most training stages.
mtp.depth.note: MTP-2 and MTP-3 are cloned from MTP-1 and trained in a lightweight post-training phase; each head is SWA + dense FFN.

mtp.modules.note: Only MTP-1 is trained in pre-training and shipped in the Base checkpoint; MTP-2/3 are cloned from it in post-training.

mtp.block.value: gated SWA attention + dense SwiGLU FFN; H-Norm(hidden) and E-Norm(next-token embedding) concatenated, then linear projection
mtp.block.quote: MTP modules use SWA and dense FFNs.
mtp.block.note: Concat/norm layout from Figure 2; checkpoint has hnorm, enorm, eh_proj, g_proj in layer 45.

mtp.ffn.quote: Each MTP head consists of a SWA and a dense FFN

mtp.shares_embedding.note: Input embedding shared (Figure 2), output head not: the MTP layer has its own 128,896 × 4,096 head (lm_head has 128,815 rows), and with it the layer holds 809,390,336 params, the paper's 0.81B per head.

mtp.params.quote: Each MTP head consists of a SWA and a dense FFN, adding only 0.81B parameters
mtp.params.note: Per head (~0.41% of the backbone), including its own output head; the Base checkpoint contains MTP-1 only.

mtp.loss_weight.quote: The MTP loss weight is set to 0.3 in Pretraining Stage 1 and 0.1 in Pre-training Stage 2

mtp.released.note: One MTP layer (index 45; /num_nextn_predict_layers 1).

norm.type.note: Paper Fig. 2: zero-centered RMSNorm throughout; applied regardless of /zero_centered.

moe.balancing.note: Sequence-wise loss weight from §6: 1 × 10^-4; config load_balance_coeff 5e-5 is not cited by the report.

norm.type.quote: For layer normalization, we use a simplified depth-scaled sandwich norm

norm.placement.note: RMSNorm on sublayer input and output, both inside the residual branch; final RMSNorm before the LM head.

norm.residual.value: depth-scaled sandwich norm: output-RMSNorm gains initialized to 1/√L
norm.residual.quote: We depth-scale the RMSNorm gain parameters for the second RMSNorm in each layer.

norm.embedding.note: Gated by config mup_enabled (true); report eq. 39.

ctx.pretrain.quote: We use local/global attention with sliding-window size for the local layers set to 4096 and pre-training sequence length 8192.

ctx.final.quote: We trained Trinity Large at a sequence length of 256K, targeting a final context window size of 256K
ctx.final.note: Card states Base includes context extension but also lists no tuning beyond 8K; config max_position_embeddings is 262,144.

ctx.max.quote: We train to 256k context for inference at 512k.

ctx.extension.value: single stage at 256K from the final pretrained checkpoint; only global (NoPE) layers extended, SWA window 4096 and RoPE unchanged; ~117B-token long-context mix; LR cosine continued 1/10 → 1/20 of peak; CP 4
ctx.extension.quote: Adjusting only the global layers resulted in a much quicker loss recovery

train.tokens.quote: Trinity Large was pre-trained on 17 trillion tokens.
train.tokens.note: Excludes context extension (blog: 33-day pretraining figure excludes it).

train.optimizer.value: Muon + AdamW (Muon for hidden layers, AdamW for embedding and output; Muon LR × max(1, √(fan_out/fan_in)))
train.optimizer.quote: we use the Muon optimizer [Jordan et al., 2024a] for hidden layers and the AdamW optimizer [Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019] for the embedding and output layers.
train.optimizer.note: Distributed Muon from the Dion repository; expert gradients orthogonalized batched per expert (§3.3).

train.lr_peak.quote: The peak learning rates are 8.0 × 10−4 for Muon and 2.0 × 10−4 for AdamW.

train.lr_min.quote: we continue cosine decay from 10 1 1 to 20 of the peak learning rate
train.lr_min.note: Muon, end of context extension (1/20 of peak); end of pretraining 8.0e-5. AdamW: 2.0e-5, then 1.0e-5.

train.schedule.value: WSD: 2000-step linear warmup, constant, cosine decay to 1/10 of peak; context extension continues cosine 1/10 → 1/20
train.schedule.quote: During the decay phase, we use a cosine decay to 10 1 of the peak learning rate
train.schedule.note: The 10T TrueBase checkpoint has no LR anneal (blog), so decay starts after 10T.

train.warmup.quote: Trinity Large. We use a linear warmup of 2000 steps.

train.batch.value: 12,288 × 8,192 (101M tokens), raised to 16,384 × 8,192 (134M tokens) after 4.9T tokens
train.batch.quote: We train with global batch size 12288 at sequence length 8192, and increase the global batch size to 16384 after crossing 4.9T tokens

train.batch_tokens.quote: We train with global batch size 12288 at sequence length 8192, and increase the global batch size to 16384 after crossing 4.9T tokens
train.batch_tokens.note: 16,384 sequences × 8192 tokens, after the step-up at 4.9T (12,288 × 8192 = 100,663,296 before).

train.precision.value: BF16 (MXFP8 linear and grouped-GEMM kernels disabled after early unstable runs)
train.precision.quote: We disabled our MXFP8 kernels for linear layers and grouped GEMMs, falling back to BF16.

train.init.value: truncated normal σ=0.009 on [−3σ, 3σ] for all trainable parameters (σ = 0.5/√d); output-norm gains 1/√L
train.init.quote: We initialize all trainable parameters from a truncated normal distribution with standard deviation 0.009.

train.stability.value: QK-norm; sigmoid attention-output gate; depth-scaled sandwich norm; z-loss 1e-6 (introduced mid-training); sequence-wise aux loss 1e-4; SMEBU; 6 dense layers; intra-document masking; BF16; random sequential document buffer from phase 3
train.stability.quote: and had to reduce the weight to 1 × 10−6 , as larger values destabilized the network.
train.stability.note: A bug left z-loss at 0 until it was introduced mid-run; the six §6 fixes were applied together after collapsed-expert restarts.

train.masking.quote: but Trinity Large was pre-trained using intra-doc attention masking.

train.data.value: DatologyAI 20T-token mix in 3 phases (13T/4T/3T), shifting from web toward code, math, STEM; >8T synthetic (~6.5T rephrased web, ~1T multilingual, ~800B code); 14 non-English languages
train.data.quote: DatologyAI generated over 8 trillion tokens of synthetic web, code, and STEM data.
train.data.note: 13T/4T/3T is the 20T mix; the report says the 17T were sampled 13:4:3 from it, the blog gives trained phases of 10T, 4T and 3T.

train.hardware.value: 2048 B300; HSDP (FSDP group 128) + EP 8; pretraining 33 days
train.hardware.at: Trinity Large blog; Training at scale
train.hardware.quote: The full pretraining run finished in 33 days.
train.hardware.note: Report §3.3: 2048 B300, FSDP group 128, EP 8, CP 4 for context extension.

train.accelerators.quote: Hardware: 2,048 NVIDIA B300 GPUs

train.parallelism.quote: For all models, we set the FSDP group size to 128. For Trinity Large, we set the EP group size to 8.

value.name: phase 1
value.note: Report: 13T of the 20T mix, from which the 17T were sampled 13:4:3; blog: 10T. Warmup then constant LR; batch 16,384 after 4.9T.
value.quote: The 17 trillion tokens that Trinity Large was trained on were sampled proportionally from the 20T mix (i.e. a 13:4:3 ratio across the three phases).

value.name: phase 2
value.note: Report: 4T of the 20T mix; blog: 4T. Shifted toward code, math and STEM.
value.quote: The 20 trillion mix was distributed across 13T tokens in phase 1, 4T tokens in phase 2, and 3T tokens in phase 3.

value.name: phase 3
value.note: Report: 3T of the 20T mix; blog: 3T. Random sequential document buffer enabled; LR ends at 1/10 of peak.
value.quote: we introduce a document buffer mid-way through the Trinity Large training run, right before beginning phase 3.

value.name: context extension
value.note: ~117B-token long-context dataset; cosine continued to 4.0e-5 (Muon).
value.quote: Our long-context extension dataset comprises approximately 117 billion tokens across 35.6 million documents.

scaling.parametrization.value: Muon LR × max(1, √(fan_out/fan_in)) for width transfer; embedding ×√d; init σ = 0.5/√d
scaling.parametrization.quote: Empirically, we observe that this adjustment enables optimal learning rate transfer when scaling model width, for Muon.
scaling.parametrization.note: The report does not name a parametrization; config mup_enabled gates the √d embedding scale.

scaling.ladder.value: Trinity Nano (6B-A1B, 56 layers, d 1024) and Trinity Mini (26B-A3B, 32 layers, d 2048), 10T tokens each
scaling.ladder.quote: serve as steps in our scaling ladder that validate the data pipeline, architecture, training recipe, and infrastructure required for Trinity Large.

eval.aa_index.at: Artificial Analysis model page /models/trinity-large-thinking, Wayback snapshot 2026-10-19
eval.aa_index.quote: Trinity Large Thinking scores 11 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
eval.aa_index.note: Score of Trinity-Large-Thinking, post-trained from this base. Variant: Trinity Large Thinking. Index v4.3.2.

params.counted_total.formula: embedding + output head + all experts + other weights, arcee-ai/Trinity-Large-Base@b2a665b safetensors headers; reproduces stated total (backbone) and active (with output head)

params.counted_embedding.formula: input embedding + output head, arcee-ai/Trinity-Large-Base@b2a665b safetensors headers

params.counted_non_embedding.formula: dense + routed backbone weights; excludes input embedding, output head, lookup tables, MTP and other modalities, arcee-ai/Trinity-Large-Base@b2a665b safetensors headers; reproduces stated total (backbone) and active (with output head)

params.counted_max_layer.formula: max(sum of dense and routed weights sharing a full layers.<index> tensor path), all experts included, arcee-ai/Trinity-Large-Base@b2a665b safetensors headers

params.counted_active_non_embedding.formula: non-expert weights + routed experts × 4/256, excluding embedding and output head, arcee-ai/Trinity-Large-Base@b2a665b safetensors headers; reproduces stated total (backbone) and active (with output head)

kv.growth_per_token.formula: 61440 B / 1 tokens (Global KV); uniform BF16, payload only; quantization overhead excluded. Global KV: 15 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry; SWA KV: 45 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry

kv.bytes_at_context.formula: 61440 B × 131072 (Global KV) + 184320 B × min(131072, 4096) (SWA KV); uniform BF16, payload only; quantization overhead excluded. Global KV: 15 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry; SWA KV: 45 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry

kv.bytes_per_token.formula: kv.bytes_at_context / 131072 tokens; uniform BF16, payload only; quantization overhead excluded. Global KV: 15 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry; SWA KV: 45 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry

kv.bytes_per_token_per_active.formula: kv.bytes_per_token (131072 tokens) / (params.active / 1e9); uniform BF16, payload only; quantization overhead excluded. Global KV: 15 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry; SWA KV: 45 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry

kv.bytes_at_context_per_active.formula: kv.bytes_at_context (131072 tokens) / (params.active / 1e9); uniform BF16, payload only; quantization overhead excluded. Global KV: 15 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry; SWA KV: 45 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry

kv.formula: Global KV: 15 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry; SWA KV: 45 × (2048 × 16/8) B/entry
